what_it_does: Large language models (LLMs) running on hardware must balance three competing demands: small area (low chip cost), low power consumption, and accurate results. This paper explores how different number formats—integer, floating-point, posit (a newer number system), logarithmic number system, and others—plus different ways to build the multiply-accumulate units (the tiny arithmetic cores that do the core math) affect these tradeoffs. By evaluating over 35,000 different hardware designs, the researchers identify which combinations are genuinely worth considering (the Pareto frontier), showing hardware designers which options give the best performance-per-watt and accuracy for their specific chip constraints.
